composition: headline centred at top inside a dimensioned frame
four equipment groups left to right along one horizontal band
a single thick pipe enters at left edge and exits at right edge, dipping and rising between groups
section labels float above each group; one label repeated below (duplicate 'PW generation', 'Monitoring and controls')
drawing-sheet border with corner ticks around the whole canvas
layout_devices: instrument loop lines dropping from gauges to a control box
labels above equipment with no cards
palette: translucent steel-blue fill inside the main pipe
typography: light-weight sans headline drawn as outline/hollow strokes
regular light sans for section labels, white on navy
tiny condensed dimension figures on dimension lines
rendering: flat, no shading except a soft translucent pipe fill
thin hairline strokes about 1 to 1.5 px
line_and_texture: thicker double-line pipe with semi-transparent fill
motifs: twin pretreatment pressure vessels with valves
RO skid with membrane housings and control panel
cylindrical PP storage tank labelled PP
loop piping with valves around the tank
dial gauges and a flow meter in-line
control panel boxes with a trend curve
ui_patterns: horizontal step rail implied by the four zones
motion_implied: water travels the pipe left to right
each zone lights as the flow reaches it
trend curve draws in the monitor box
t2i_keywords: one continuous pipe running left to right
drawing sheet border with corner ticks
four zones in a horizontal row
t2i_prompt: A wide web page section rendered as an engineering blueprint on a deep navy background. A single continuous pipe with a soft translucent steel-blue fill enters from the left edge and runs to the right edge, passing through a row of isometric process equipment drawn in pale blue-white hairline line art: <CONTENT>. Each group has a short light sans-serif label above it; small steel-blue arrows show flow direction. Dimension lines with tick marks span each zone, a thin drawing-sheet border with corner ticks frames the canvas, and a light thin headline sits centred at the top. Flat, no shading, no people, straight-on view.
signature_idea: The whole offer drawn as one blueprint pipe that physically threads every system in order, so 'one package' is literally one line.
strengths: communicates the integrated package at a glance: one line, four stops
equipment is recognisable to process engineers (vessels, skid, tank, gauges)
navy and pale line palette is close to brand
pipe-as-timeline is a strong animation hook
weaknesses: duplicated labels ('PW generation', 'Monitoring and controls') show generator confusion
outlined headline looks like a dated blueprint cliché and is hard to read
dense, evenly weighted detail with little negative space
no limestone or paper-white surface, so the page would feel heavy
blueprint-on-navy is a common engineering trope
brand_fit_why: Navy, hairlines and steel-blue line accent match the brand, but it is busy, uses a hollow display headline instead of Geist light, and treats space as filler rather than material.
